guides.title: Fix "No Service" and SOS Mode on Your Phone in Rural Areas
guides.summary: Your phone says No Service or shows SOS only. Nine things to try, in order, before you assume there is no signal at all.
guides.quick_fix: Turn Airplane Mode ON for 15 seconds, then OFF. That forces the phone to re-scan for towers and clears most No Service and SOS glitches on the spot.
prerequisites: Your phone, charged enough to make a call
The phone passcode, if you use one
Two minutes somewhere you have had signal before, if you can move
guides.dont_need: You do not need to reset the phone, reinstall anything, or call your carrier yet. Try these first.
verification: The signal bars are back in the top corner
No Service and SOS are gone from the status bar
You can place a test call (call your own voicemail and hang up)
If Wi-Fi Calling is on, calls work even at one bar
escalation: Reset Network Settings (iPhone: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings; Android: Settings > System > Reset > Reset Wi-Fi, mobile and Bluetooth). This forgets saved Wi-Fi passwords, so have them handy.
Power the phone off, remove the SIM tray with the pin tool, reseat the card, and power back on. Skip this if your phone uses an eSIM.
Move the SIM into another phone to prove whether the trouble is the phone or the network.
Ask a neighbour on the same carrier whether their phone is working right now.
Check your carrier coverage map and report the dead zone so it is on record.

faq.q: Does SOS mean I can still call 911?
faq.a: Yes. On iPhone and most Android phones, SOS means emergency calls will use any available carrier, not just yours. Leave it on if you are somewhere risky.

faq.q: Why does my phone lose signal in the same spot every time?
faq.a: That is a real dead zone rather than a glitch. It is usually terrain, distance from the tower, or the walls of the building. Wi-Fi Calling is the fix that helps most at home.

faq.q: Would a new phone get better signal?
faq.a: Only if the problem is your phone antenna. Test your SIM in another phone first. If that phone also shows No Service, a new phone will not help.

guides.title: Satellite Internet Slow or Dropping Out (Starlink & HughesNet)
guides.summary: Why satellite internet slows down, drops out, and stalls in bad weather — and the settings and placement fixes that actually help.
guides.quick_fix: Check the dish for snow, dust, or a new obstruction (a growing tree) and clear it. Then run the app's own speed test. Most satellite slowdowns are obstruction or weather, not a setting.
prerequisites: The Starlink or HughesNet app on your phone
The Wi-Fi password for your router
A clear line of sight check — can you see the dish from the ground
guides.dont_need: You do not need to reboot the dish to factory settings, or buy a new router. Most fixes are placement and weather.
verification: A speed test inside the app shows your normal range for the plan
The obstruction view in the app shows a clear, dark sky area
Video calls hold for five minutes without freezing
No red or yellow alerts on the app's home screen
escalation: Power-cycle the dish: unplug it at the wall for a full 60 seconds, then plug it back in and let it re-acquire (up to 15 minutes).
Move the router away from the dish's power supply and away from microwaves and cordless phone bases.
Run an ethernet cable from the router straight to one device to prove whether the slowdown is Wi-Fi or the satellite link itself.
Contact support with your speed test history and the exact times the slowdown happens — evenings and storms are normal and worth documenting.

faq.q: Why is satellite internet slow in the evening?
faq.a: Everyone in your area is online at once, and the satellite capacity is shared. This is congestion, not a fault. It is worst between about 7pm and 11pm.

faq.q: Does weather really break satellite internet?
faq.a: Yes. Heavy rain, wet snow, and thick cloud attenuate the signal. Light rain usually does not. This is called rain fade and it is physics, not a broken dish.

faq.q: How much does latency matter?
faq.a: A lot for video calls and gaming. Satellite round-trips run much higher than cable, so a stable 50 Mbps on satellite can feel worse than 15 Mbps on cable for live calls.

guides.title: Boost Home Wi-Fi Across a Large House and Outbuildings
guides.summary: Get Wi-Fi to the far bedroom, the shop, and the barn without buying the wrong gadget. Where to put the router, and when a mesh or a bridge is the right call.
guides.quick_fix: Move the router out of the cupboard and off the floor, up high and central to the rooms that matter. Wi-Fi is blocked by metal, concrete and water — a cupboard is the usual cause of a dead zone.
prerequisites: Access to your router (the box your internet comes from)
Your Wi-Fi network name and password
A phone to walk around and test signal with
guides.dont_need: You do not need to buy a booster or a mesh kit until you have tried moving the router and testing. Half of all dead zones are placement.
verification: Signal bars hold up in the room that used to be dead
A video streams in the far room without buffering
The device shows the 5 GHz network when you are close, and 2.4 GHz when you are far
Speed test in the far room is at least half of what you get beside the router
escalation: Log into the router and separate the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz network names so you can choose. 2.4 GHz reaches further; 5 GHz is faster but shorter.
Change the Wi-Fi channel to 1, 6, or 11 on 2.4 GHz if neighbours' networks are crowding you.
Add a mesh system for one building — a set of two or three units is far better than a single booster.
Use a point-to-point wireless bridge for a separate outbuilding. This is the correct tool for a shop or barn 50 feet or more away, and it is not the same thing as a Wi-Fi booster.

faq.q: Should I buy a Wi-Fi booster or a mesh system?
faq.a: Mesh, almost always. A single booster repeats a signal it already received weakly, which halves your speed. A mesh system connects the units properly and keeps the speed up.

faq.q: Why is the far room slow but shows full bars?
faq.a: Bars show the connection to the router, not the speed of it. A far-away device can hold on with strong bars at a slow speed. Test the actual speed, not the bars.

faq.q: How do I get Wi-Fi to a detached shop or barn?
faq.a: Use a point-to-point wireless bridge (two small units aimed at each other) or run a cable if you can. A booster inside the house will not reach it.

guides.title: Clear Cache, Cookies and Pop-Ups in Any Browser
guides.summary: A slow, cluttered browser and constant pop-ups are usually the same problem. Clear the right things in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox without losing your passwords.
guides.quick_fix: Open a private or incognito window and load the same site. If it works there, it is your cache or cookies. That one test tells you whether clearing will help before you clear anything.
prerequisites: A few minutes
Your password manager, or a note of your important passwords
The browser you actually use
guides.dont_need: You do not need to clear saved passwords or bookmarks. Leave those ticked off and you will stay signed in to almost everything.
verification: The page that was broken loads correctly
Pop-ups stop appearing on sites you trust
The browser feels quicker on heavy pages
You are still signed in to your email and bank
escalation: Turn on the browser's pop-up blocker (Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Site settings > Pop-ups and redirects).
Remove suspicious extensions: Settings > Extensions. Anything you do not recognise, turn off.
Reset the browser's settings to default as a last resort — this keeps bookmarks but clears the rest.
If pop-ups appear even with the browser closed, run a malware scan. That is not a browser problem.

faq.q: Will clearing cookies sign me out of everything?
faq.a: Out of most sites, yes. That is why you should leave Passwords unticked and keep a password manager so signing back in is painless.

faq.q: What is the difference between cache and cookies?
faq.a: Cache is saved pieces of pages that make loading faster. Cookies are small notes sites leave to remember you. Clearing cache fixes broken pages. Clearing cookies fixes sign-in and tracking oddities.

faq.q: Do I need to clear my history too?
faq.a: No. History is just a list. It does not slow the browser down, and clearing it only loses you the ability to find a page you visited earlier.

guides.title: Password Recovery and Setting Up a Password Manager with 2FA
guides.summary: Get back into a locked account, then set up a password manager and two-factor so it never happens again. Written for people who have never used one.
guides.quick_fix: Before anything else, find the account's own Forgot password link and use the email or phone number you signed up with. Do not use a reset link from an email you did not ask for.
prerequisites: Access to the email address the account uses
Your phone, for verification codes
About 25 minutes, done calmly
guides.dont_need: You do not need to write passwords on paper, and you do not need to change every password today. Start with email, then bank, then everything else.
verification: You are signed in to the account you were locked out of
The password manager fills a login for you on a test site
Two-factor codes arrive and work
You have saved your recovery codes somewhere offline
escalation: If the reset email never arrives, check the spam and junk folders, and search your inbox for the account name.
If the account uses a phone number you no longer have, use the account's account-recovery form rather than the normal reset.
If you are locked out of your email itself, call the provider's support line — email is the master key, so it is worth the phone call.
If you believe the account was taken over, change the email password first, then everything else, then check the account's forwarding and recovery settings for anything you did not add.

faq.q: Which password manager should I use?
faq.a: A well-known one that syncs across your devices and has a free tier. Bitwarden is free and open-source. 1Password and Dashlane are paid and polished. Your browser's built-in one is better than nothing but weaker than a dedicated app.

faq.q: Is a password manager safe if they get hacked?
faq.a: A good one stores your passwords encrypted with a key only you hold, so a break-in at the company does not expose them. That is the whole point of the design.

faq.q: What is two-factor, in one sentence?
faq.a: A second proof that it is really you — a code from an app or a text — on top of your password, so a stolen password alone is not enough.

faq.q: Should I use text messages for 2FA?
faq.a: It is far better than nothing, but an authenticator app is stronger because text messages can be intercepted. Use the app when the site offers it.

guides.title: Quick Fixes for an Extremely Slow Computer or Laptop
guides.summary: The eight things that actually speed up a slow Windows PC or Mac, in order of effort — from what starts automatically to the drive that is quietly full.
guides.quick_fix: Restart the computer properly — Start menu, Restart — rather than closing the lid. Then open Task Manager or Activity Monitor and see what is using the most memory. One runaway program is often the whole problem.
prerequisites: About half an hour
The computer plugged in, not on battery
Permission to install updates
guides.dont_need: You do not need to buy more memory yet, and you do not need to reinstall Windows. Work down this list first.
verification: The computer starts up in under two minutes
Opening a browser and a document no longer freezes
The drive has at least 15 percent free space
Task Manager shows no single program pinned near 100 percent
escalation: Check the drive type. If the computer still has a spinning hard disk rather than an SSD, replacing it with an SSD is the single biggest speed upgrade available and is often cheaper than a new machine.
Run a full malware scan with the built-in tool (Windows Security or a reputable scanner). Adware is a very common cause of a slow machine.
Check for a failing drive: run the manufacturer's health tool. A drive that is dying makes everything slow and is worth catching early.
If it is a work machine or over five years old, weigh the cost of an SSD and more memory against a replacement.

faq.q: How much free space does Windows need?
faq.a: Keep at least 15 percent of the drive free. Windows uses free space for updates and temporary files, and a drive above 90 percent full will feel slow no matter what else you do.

faq.q: Will more memory make it faster?
faq.a: It helps if Task Manager shows memory pinned near the top. If the disk or the processor is the bottleneck, more memory will not help and you would be wasting money.

faq.q: Does a factory reset fix a slow computer?
faq.a: Sometimes, but it is a last resort. Work through this list first — a reset wipes your programs and takes hours, and it is often unnecessary.

guides.title: Connect a Smart TV or Streaming Stick to Weak Wi-Fi
guides.summary: Stop the buffering on a smart TV or streaming stick that sits too far from the router. The settings that help, and the cheap cable that beats all of them.
guides.quick_fix: Restart the router and the TV or stick together — unplug both, wait 30 seconds, plug the router in first, then the TV. Then check the Wi-Fi signal reading on the TV's network screen.
prerequisites: Your Wi-Fi name and password
Access to the router
The TV remote
guides.dont_need: You do not need a new TV or a new router. Most buffering is a signal problem, and the cheapest fix is usually a cable.
verification: The TV reports a strong signal on its network screen
Video plays for ten minutes without buffering
The picture settles at full quality rather than staying blurry
The streaming app opens in a few seconds
escalation: Switch the TV to the 2.4 GHz network if it is far from the router — it reaches further even though it is slower.
Move the router higher and out of a cupboard, closer to the TV wall.
Move the streaming stick out of a metal TV cabinet or away from the back of the TV with a short extension cable.
Run an ethernet cable to the TV. If the TV has no port, use a powerline adapter or a Wi-Fi extender with an ethernet port, and plug the TV into that.

faq.q: Why does my phone stream fine but the TV buffers?
faq.a: The phone is usually closer and newer. The TV may have an older, weaker Wi-Fi chip, or sit behind a metal cabinet or wall. Test the TV's own signal reading rather than assuming.

faq.q: Should I use 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz for a TV?
faq.a: Use 5 GHz if the TV is in the same room as the router — it is faster. Use 2.4 GHz if the TV is across the house — it reaches further. Pick for distance, not speed.

faq.q: What is the cheapest reliable fix?
faq.a: An ethernet cable. If you cannot run one, a powerline adapter usually beats Wi-Fi and costs far less than a new TV.

guides.title: Spot and Avoid Phishing Scams, Text Spam and Robocalls
guides.summary: The five tells that give away a scam message, plus how to cut down spam texts and robocalls and what to do if you already clicked.
symptoms: someone pretending to be a bank
guides.quick_fix: If a message creates urgency — act now, account locked, package held, pay a fee — stop and contact the company using the number on your own card or statement, never the number in the message.
prerequisites: Your phone, with a few minutes to change settings
A note of which accounts you actually have
guides.dont_need: You do not need to answer a suspicious call to verify it, and you do not need to click a link to check whether it is real.
verification: Unknown-caller filtering is switched on
You can name the five tells without looking them up
Spam texts are being reported rather than replied to
You know the phone number on the back of your bank card
escalation: If you already gave out a password, change it immediately and turn on two-factor — start with email.
If you gave card details, call the number on the back of the card and ask them to freeze it.
If you installed something they told you to install, remove it and run a malware scan.
Report the message: forward spam texts to 7726 (SPAM), and report calls and emails to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

faq.q: Do real banks ever text asking me to log in?
faq.a: Almost never. A real bank may send a genuine alert, but it will never ask you to click a link and enter your full password. When in doubt, call the number on your card.

faq.q: What is the one rule that catches most scams?
faq.a: Urgency. Scams need you to act before you think. Any message that pressures you to act right now is worth slowing down on, every single time.

faq.q: Should I reply STOP to spam texts?
faq.a: Do not reply at all. Replying confirms your number is live and can invite more. Report it instead, and block the sender.

guides.title: Set Up a Wireless Printer and Fix Printer Offline Errors
guides.summary: Get a wireless printer onto your network once and keep it there. Plus the offline-error fixes, in order, when it drops off again.
guides.quick_fix: Check the printer is awake and on the same Wi-Fi as your computer, then turn the printer off and on. A printer that has gone to sleep loses its network address and reports itself offline.
prerequisites: The printer and your Wi-Fi password
Access to the router
Ten quiet minutes
guides.dont_need: You do not need to reinstall the printer from scratch unless the steps below fail. Try the simple fixes first.
verification: The printer shows as ready rather than offline
A test page prints
The printer has the same network name as your computer
It survives a sleep and wake cycle without going offline again
escalation: Give the printer a fixed address. In the router settings, reserve an IP address for the printer so it stops changing.
Remove the printer from your computer and add it again by its address rather than by name.
Connect by USB once to confirm the printer works at all, then return to Wi-Fi.
Update the printer firmware from the printer's own menu or the manufacturer's app.

faq.q: Why does my printer keep going offline?
faq.a: Almost always because it was given a new network address when it woke up, and the computer is still looking for the old one. Reserving a fixed address in the router stops this for good.

faq.q: Should I use 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz for a printer?
faq.a: 2.4 GHz, nearly always. Most printers only support 2.4 GHz, and it reaches further. Check your printer's spec sheet if you are unsure.

faq.q: The printer shows up twice — which do I use?
faq.a: Remove both and add one. Duplicate entries are usually one old USB install and one network install, and the computer keeps picking the wrong one.

guides.title: Move Your Photos and Files to a New Device and Set Up Cloud Backup
guides.summary: Get everything off the old phone or computer and onto the new one without losing photos — then set up a backup that actually runs on its own.
symptoms: do not know where photos went
guides.quick_fix: Before you do anything, copy the photos off the old device to somewhere else — a computer or an external drive. Once they are safe in two places, the rest of the move is relaxed.
prerequisites: Both devices, charged and on Wi-Fi
The account password for the old device
A spare hour, done calmly
guides.dont_need: You do not need to wipe the old device yet. Keep it until the new one is working and you have checked your photos are there.
verification: The photo count on the new device matches the old one
You can open an old photo on the new device
A file from the old computer opens on the new one
A backup has run on its own at least once
escalation: If the new device runs out of storage, move photos to an external drive or cloud and keep only recent ones on the device.
If a transfer app stalls, do it in batches — photos first, then documents, then everything else.
If an old device will not turn on, remove its storage drive and read it with a USB adapter, or take it to a shop before disposing of it.
If cloud storage is full, either upgrade the plan or use an external drive — do not delete the only copy.

faq.q: Where did my photos go when I got a new phone?
faq.a: If they were in iCloud or Google Photos, they download again when you sign in. If they were only on the old phone, they moved nowhere and you must copy them across yourself.

faq.q: Is the cloud the same as a backup?
faq.a: Not quite. A cloud library syncs — if you delete a photo in one place, it deletes everywhere. A backup keeps a separate copy you can restore. Use both.

faq.q: Should I erase the old device?
faq.a: Only after the new one is fully working and you have checked the photos. Keep the old device for a week or two as your safety net.
